metadata.title: Quantitative persistence in a fixed-city area equation
metadata.description:
For every fixed finite collection of at least two distinct interior sites in the unit square and every strictly positive initial probability vector, consider the hard weighted-Voronoi area equation z_i prime = A_i(z) - z_i, where city i maximizes z_i^alpha times distance to the power -beta. We give a quantitative all-coordinate persistence theorem when beta > 2 alpha: an explicit time-dependent lower bound, a positive bound for all time, and a positive limiting inferior bound independent of the starting state. An asymmetric three-city instance with alpha=2, beta=8 has every share between 1/4096 and 2047/2048 for all nonnegative time. This refutes the unrestricted alpha > 1 collapse alternative in the literal 2007 Conjecture 32(a) and the catalog conjunction containing it. The result does not establish convergence, equilibrium uniqueness, initial-value independence of a limit, or stochastic city-founding conclusions. Zero initial weights, coincident sites, boundary sites, and the one-city case are outside the stated theorem.

The model and conjecture are Aldous's. Multiplicatively weighted Voronoi/Apollonius geometry is classical; the original 2007 notes already contain the protected-neighborhood mechanism and area exponent 2 alpha / beta in an unfinished stochastic argument. The scalar substitution and integrating-factor step are standard. Ferudun's unrefereed preprint, stated release 14 October 2026, explicitly gives robust two-city Conjecture 32(a) counterexamples in another parameter range and records the ratio-invariance inconsistency. Its proved every-exponent derivative lemma and position continuity also imply qualitative two-city noncollapse in the present beta > 2 alpha regime. These overlapping conclusions receive direct credit. The present theorem supplies all-site, all-positive-initial-state quantitative persistence; it is not advertised as the first negative answer or as a new geometric method. The original complete PR was recorded on 6 October 2026, but chronology and bounded searches certify neither firstness, exhaustive novelty nor worldwide current openness.

The deposit contains a five-page research note and a verification archive with editable source, all forty frozen original files, original nested evidence archives, independent analytical and bounded priority audit evidence, source version/hash locators, an externally pinned closed-inventory verifier and deterministic ZIP builder. Default finite replay runs the original witness/checker self-tests under normal and optimized Python. Optional full provenance requires three complete pinned corpora and two separately supplied primary PDFs. Primary publications, extracted source text, page images, raw dataset records and private credentials are excluded. Artifact hashes and finite checks do not certify the analytic theorem or priority. Compressed-byte reproducibility is limited to identical inputs and the same Python ZIP implementation and zlib runtime.

OpenAI tools were used extensively in solving, proof development, drafting, coding, reproduction and adversarial checking. This is an unrefereed preprint; no completed external human peer review or formal proof-assistant verification is claimed. The author is responsible for the claims.

abstract_and_description_contract.complete_original_abstract_tex: For finitely many fixed distinct interior sites in the unit square, let each site's positive population share grow at the rate of the area where its influence is maximal, minus its current share. Influence is proportional to population to the power $\alpha$ times distance to the power $-\beta$. We prove that every positive initial probability vector gives a global trajectory and, when $\beta>2\alpha$, every share has an explicit positive lower bound for all time. An asymmetric three-site instance with $\alpha=2$ and $\beta=8$ has all shares between $1/4096$ and $2047/2048$. This disproves the unrestricted $\alpha>1$ collapse alternative in the literal 2007 fixed-city conjecture. The result is a quantitative, all-site persistence statement; it does not establish convergence or resolve the stochastic city-founding model. We credit the original local geometric mechanism and a directly overlapping 2026 two-city counterexample analysis. No firstness claim is made.

full_source_claim_expectations_not_new_v.equation: D=[0,1]^2; n>=2 fixed distinct interior sites x_i in (0,1)^2; α,β>0. S_i(z)={y in D:z_i^α |y-x_i|^(-β)>=z_j^α |y-x_j|^(-β) for every j}; A_i(z)=area(S_i(z)); dz_i/dt=A_i(z)-z_i. Finite-site/tie-boundary conventions do not affect area.
full_source_claim_expectations_not_new_v.initial_state: Strictly positive probability vector z(0) in Delta°: all coordinates positive and sum1.
full_source_claim_expectations_not_new_v.global_trajectory_source_claim: Unique global positive classical trajectory for every positive initial probability vector, for all α,β>0. Local Lipschitz regularity on the positive orthant includes equal weights; this does not assert uniqueness on the closed boundary.
full_source_claim_expectations_not_new_v.ratio_parameters: q=α/β; p=2q. Dominance becomes |y-x_i|<=(z_i/z_j)^q |y-x_j| for ALL competitors. Cells and vector field depend only on q, with NO time change.
full_source_claim_expectations_not_new_v.geometric_constants: Choose h_i>0 with x_i+[-h_i,h_i]^2 contained in D and 8h_i^2<=|x_i-x_j|^2 for every j!=i. Set K_i=4h_i^2; constants need not be optimal.
full_source_claim_expectations_not_new_v.dependence_and_limit: The all-time lower bound depends on the initial value; the positive asymptotic lower bound does not. A limiting inferior is not a limit or convergence assertion.
proof_explanation_contract: Classical multiplicatively weighted Voronoi/Apollonius cells have null pairwise tie sets. A quantitative band-area estimate gives local Lipschitz dependence, including equal-weight line boundaries.
The normalized simplex is invariant; z_i(t)>=exp(-t)z_i(0) gives positivity and finite-time global continuation.
The protected square Q_i=x_i+[-h_i z_i^q,h_i z_i^q]^2 lies in the ACTUAL winning cell against every competitor simultaneously.
Thus A_i(z)>=K_i z_i^p. The standard substitution u_i=z_i^(1-p) yields du_i/dt >= (1-p)(K_i-u_i), integrated by a standard integrating factor.
The full trajectory bound is analytic; rational certificate checks and samples do not establish all-time persistence.

exact_asymmetric_instance.all_time_bounds: 1/4096<=z_i(t)<=2047/2048 for all three coordinates and every t>=0
exact_asymmetric_instance.status: Manuscript source assertion only; no new arithmetic/program execution here.

full_source_claim_expectations_not_new_v.literal_conjecture_scope: The target is Aldous 2007 rough notes §6.4, Conjecture32(a), p40, with global positive α,β parameter declaration p2: collapse predicted if α>1 OR0<β<2α for unspecified general-position data. The source refutes the UNRESTRICTED α>1 alternative on the open region α>1,β>2α, all distinct interior configurations/all positive initial vectors. It does not silently assume or prove convergence.
full_source_claim_expectations_not_new_v.later_model_distinction: The later Aldous–Huang2012 stochastic city-founding model declares0<α<=1 and does not state this fixed-city conjecture; the source does not refute that later stochastic model.
excluded_or_unproved: No persistence assertion at β=2α or β<2α.
No convergence, unique positive equilibrium or initial-value independence of a limiting state.
No conclusion for stochastic founding of new cities.
Coincident sites, boundary sites, zero initial weights and the one-city case are outside the theorem.
Do not present unspecified general-position language as excluding this open class of counterexamples.

attribution_overlap_priority_status_cont.Ferudun_overlap_as_source_assertion: Ferudun unrefereed14October2026 preprint DOI10.5281/zenodo.23367464 explicitly supplies robust two-city counterexamples in another range1<=p<sqrt(3) (with α>1 onp1). Proved every-exponent derivative lemma f_prime(1/2)=p(a+1/(12a)) and positional continuity imply qualitative two-city noncollapse also for0<p<1: a=1/4 gives7p/12<1. Its quantitative strip extension is labeled a sketch; the source credits the qualitative consequence of proved lemmas rather than treating the sketch as proved. No first negative answer claim.
attribution_overlap_priority_status_cont.present_contribution_scope: Quantitative persistence for ALL sites and ALL strictly positive initial probability vectors, distinguished from local two-city basins.
attribution_overlap_priority_status_cont.ratio_invariance_credit: Ferudun also records ratio invariance. (α,β)=(2,8) and(1/2,2) yield the same vector field. Incompatibility of the two literal conjecture clauses alone does not identify which fails; the persistence theorem directly rules out collapse.
